title: Introduce credential-swapper and resumable line-buffered streams (cross-SDK)
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a CredentialSwapper abstraction and a resumable LineBufferedAsyncIterator across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Improves robustness for interrupted streams and provides a delegated token fallback order. Patches include small ergonomic surface wins (simpler stream resumption, clearer error classes) and minor version bumps for each SDK. Non-breaking to existing public APIs by default, opt-in behaviors documented.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see production incidents where long-lived streaming connections are interrupted during token refresh windows or due to transient network blips. Existing SDKs had ad-hoc reconnection code and differing token fallback behaviors. This PR introduces a lightweight, consistent credential swapping/fallback pipeline (CredentialSwapper) and a resumable line-buffered streaming iterator (LineBufferedAsyncIterator) implemented in Python/TypeScript/Go so application code can rely on identical semantics across languages.

What this PR does (single summary): Adds CredentialSwapper as an injectable strategy that 1) tries the active token, 2) transparently falls back to a delegated refresh token, and 3) invokes a user-provided tokenProvider callback as last resort. Adds a stream iterator that reassembles chunked text using line delimiters (\n) into logical messages, preserves an opaque resumeToken, and supports manual or automatic resume on reconnect. Also bumps SDK versions (py 1.13.0, ts 1.9.1, go v0.7.4) and updates a selection of examples and docs.

Testing notes: Unit coverage added for primary code paths: token present, delegated refresh success, provider callback invoked, and resumeToken replay resulting in duplicate suppression. E2E harness runs the new flaky-network scenario that simulates TCP resets mid-chunk and ensures resume occurs without duplication or deadlock. Performance microbenchmarks show <2% overhead on steady-state token checks (cached path), a ~5-8% increase in allocation during active resume sequences (acceptable for resumed sessions).

Review conversation (selected highlights):
- Lucas Chen (review): "CredentialSwapper looks solid. Two asks: (1) make the tokenProvider callback optional by default and (2) add a short-circuit path when token TTL > 30s to avoid unnecessary refreshes."
- Priya (author): "Implemented optional tokenProvider default; added TTL short-circuit and tests. See commit 7af3d2a."
- Sofia Petrova (review): "LineBufferedAsyncIterator is a good ergonomics win. Can we expose a MaxBufferBytes option so users can avoid OOM on pathological streams?"
- Priya: "Added max_buffer_bytes option with safe default 64KiB; iterator returns explicit BufferOverflowError when exceeded. Updated docs and examples."
- Hiro Tanaka (review): "Go implementation: prefer context cancellation propagation — add ctx checks on each chunk assemble path."
- Priya: "Go changes updated to propagate ctx cancellation; added test that cancels mid-resume and verifies cleanup."
- CI / infra note: an intermittent flake in the TS stream-resume test was resolved by increasing the test harness timeout and adding deterministic sequence IDs.

Decision notes and tradeoffs: We purposely made CredentialSwapper an abstraction rather than changing existing token stores to retain backward compatibility and allow gradual opt-in for clients that want explicit delegated fallback. LineBufferedAsyncIterator targets line-delimited protocols (the most common for our streaming outputs) — future work may add delimited-by-token or JSON-aware reassembly.

Migration guidance: Existing client code continues to work unchanged. To opt-in: instantiate SDK client with credentialSwapper option and/or use the new stream.iterator = LineBufferedAsyncIterator.fromResponse(resp) helper. Examples in docs/quickstarts show migration steps and code samples for Python/TS/Go.

- Consider adding a shared telemetry event for resume attempts to correlate server-side logs.
- Evaluate making CredentialSwapper the default behavior for dedicated/private deployments later this quarter.
